title: Canonicalize URLs for an exact origin policy
prompt: Implement solve(payload) for allowed_origins and urls (lists of strings), with no network access. Accept only absolute ASCII http/https URLs with a host, no username/password, no backslash, no whitespace/control characters (ASCII <=32 or 127). An authority must be a DNS host or bracketed IPv6 host followed by at most one colon and a nonempty decimal port; extra text after a closing IPv6 bracket is invalid. Ports must be integers 1..65535; absent ports use 80 or 443. Normalize scheme and DNS hostname to lowercase, remove exactly one trailing DNS dot, and omit the default port. DNS labels use letters/digits/hyphens, start/end alphanumeric, length 1..63, total host length 1..253; numeric labels are allowed. Bracketed IPv6 is accepted and normalized to lowercase compressed form; zone identifiers are rejected. Canonical origin is scheme://host[:nondefaultport], with IPv6 brackets preserved. Target paths, queries and fragments do not affect origin. allowed_origins must additionally have path empty or "/", and no nonempty query or fragment; any invalid allowlist entry returns {"error":"invalid_origin"} before checking targets. Return {"results":[{"origin":canonical_string_or_null,"allowed":boolean},...]} in target order; invalid targets get null/false, valid ones require exact canonical origin membership. Empty target lists are valid. Any numeric inputs are finite; inputs have the documented shapes; unspecified validation is out of scope. Do not mutate payload or any nested value. Numeric absolute tolerance 0, relative tolerance 0; strings, booleans, errors and collection shapes must match exactly.
bad_solution:
def solve(payload):
    return {"results": [{"origin": value.split("/",3)[0]+"//"+value.split("/")[2], "allowed": any(value.startswith(origin) for origin in payload["allowed_origins"])} for value in payload["urls"]]}
